content.overview: Environmental Impact Assessment is the process of evaluating the likely environmental effects of a proposed project before a decision is taken to grant environmental clearance. In India the framework is primarily statutory under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the EIA Notification issued by the Central Government. Projects are screened and categorised; public consultation and appraisal stages apply as the notification requires. Operating without required clearance, or in breach of conditions, attracts statutory consequences.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is the project in a category requiring EIA/clearance? (2) Screening and appraisal complete? (3) Public consultation where required? (4) Clearance conditions complied with?
content.study:
EIA is a preventive tool aligned with the precautionary principle. Always check the current EIA Notification and amendments for category lists, exemption and process steps — do not invent category numbers from memory.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Assess likely environmental impacts before clearance so that harm can be avoided, mitigated or conditioned.

sections.heading: Legal base
sections.body: EPA 1986 enabling powers and the EIA Notification issued thereunder; project-specific sector clearances may also apply.

sections.heading: Process outline
sections.body: Screening, scoping, public consultation (where applicable), appraisal and decision — as the current notification provides.

sections.heading: Conditions and compliance
sections.body: Clearance is typically conditional; breach of conditions is a compliance and enforcement issue under the EPA scheme.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: Challenges may lie before NGT for Schedule I environmental questions, or High Court under Art. 226 where maintainable.

examples.title: Category project without clearance
examples.body: A project requiring prior environmental clearance under the EIA Notification proceeds without it — clearance defect and potential EPA enforcement follow.

hypotheticals.question: Is EIA optional for every industrial project?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Whether EIA/clearance is required depends on the project category under the current EIA Notification and related instruments.

distinctions.title: EIA clearance vs Water/Air consent
distinctions.left: Prior environmental clearance under EIA framework for listed projects.
distinctions.right: Medium-specific Board consent under Water Act / Air Act.

misconceptions.trap: EIA clearance replaces Water and Air Act consents.
misconceptions.correction: EIA clearance and medium-specific consents are distinct requirements; both may apply.
